correctness.rationale: For GP(10,3) with 20 vertices and 30 edges, independent exact enumeration gives 60 perfect matchings, whose full downward closure contains 44,282 faces including empty; direct union agrees with perfect-extendibility. Independent algorithm using the specified 30 edge-order toggles yields 22,124 acyclic matched pairs; all 244,830 nonempty Hasse incidences topologically sort, leaving one 0-cell, 31 critical 3-cells and one critical 4-cell. Exact signed Morse reduction of the only critical four-cell returns a 31x1 zero integer vector, not merely mod2; pi3(wedge 31 S3)=Z31 so attaching map is null and the claimed wedge follows. Source verifier further confirms 10x10 bipartite permanent=60 and all ordinary-matchings completion. No family extrapolation asserted.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is the canonical 20-vertex bipartite cubic incidence/middle-level graph and perfect extendibility is a natural matching-complex functor. Its full integral homotopy type was not implied by the ordinary matching complex or Heawood case. A complete zero-attaching-map certificate in this natural sparse graph is a meaningful finite classification despite no general GP(n,k) theorem.
